A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original CIFAR-10 experiments, gradient analyses, component and hyperparameter ablations, and results from three independent random-seed runs.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds ImageNet experiments and expanded empirical-distribution comparisons.

M1.justification: The core CIFAR-10 method remains unchanged. V3 adds an ImageNet adaptation that omits data reweighting and uses a Gaussian-pretrained model for data selection with discarding epoch zero (Appendix C.1, Table 7). The relocated Algorithm 2 otherwise has equivalent control flow.

E1.justification: V2 evaluates only CIFAR-10. V3 adds ImageNet training and certification, including comparative performance and selection-bias analysis (Table 4 and Appendix E.2), substantially broadening the empirical coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 9 extends Appendix B's four-model ECDF comparison by including SmoothAdv, SmoothMix, and MACER. These methods already appeared elsewhere in v2, but their participation in this comparison is added. The main CIFAR-10 baseline set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds ImageNet-specific settings: ResNet-50, 90 training epochs, learning-rate decay every 30 epochs, noise-sample counts of 1/1/2 across the three noise levels, and 50 samples for pretrained-model data selection. The retained CIFAR-10 settings and certification budget N = 100000 with alpha = 0.001 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 expands the ECDF case study to examine dominance across more methods and noise levels. Appendix E.2 checks whether hard-sample selection bias also occurs on ImageNet. Existing component, hyperparameter, attack-norm, and certification-budget analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard deviations from three independent random-seed runs on CIFAR-10 (v2 Table 5; v3 Table 8). V3 adds no corresponding uncertainty analysis for ImageNet. Correcting the table caption from certified radius to certified accuracy does not change the statistical reporting.

E6.justification: V3 Table 4 newly reports ImageNet ACRs of 0.529, 0.842, and 1.042; the respective best baseline values are 0.532 for SmoothAdv, 0.846 for SmoothMix, and 1.071 for CAT-RS. Expanded ECDF comparisons add qualitative findings. All ten matched numerical result tables, including CIFAR-10 ablations and seed statistics, retain identical data.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, their Appendix A proofs, and the ECDF conversion arguments retain the same mathematical substance. V3 explicitly identifies the Gaussian quantity in Theorem 2 as a probability density, consistent with the density formula already used in v2's proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the performance claim as state-of-the-art ACR on CIFAR-10 and competitive ACR on ImageNet. Summary recommendations foreground ECDF, although Section 7 retains the certified-accuracy alternative. The central criticism of ACR and recommendation to discontinue it remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now distinguishes ACR's sensitivity to easy-sample improvements from whether those improvements are easier to optimize, presenting the latter argument as an empirically supported hypothesis. V3 also explicitly limits its study to Cohen et al.'s certifier and acknowledges sound approaches using variable noise scales.

D1.justification: V3 extends the training documentation with ImageNet settings and adds repository access information for code, models, and ECDF data. It also clarifies that the gradient analysis concerns model parameters. However, Appendix C.1 omits v2's batch-size disclosure of 256; this does not establish an actual batch-size change.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a structured survey of 13 works from 2020–2024, classifying ACR use, universal accuracy improvements, SOTA claims, and model customization (Table 1). Additional certification and variable-noise literature substantially expands the positioning. Publication updates to existing references are separate bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: V3 edits the abstract and selected paragraphs, retitles Section 4.2, adds appendix subsections, and introduces reproducibility and acknowledgements statements. The main section order and overall narrative structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the literature-survey table, ImageNet results and hyperparameter tables, and two multi-panel ECDF figures. Algorithm 2 moves from the main text to Appendix C.1, and appendix displays are rearranged. This substantially expands the visual presentation while retaining the original plots and result tables.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens support for the field-wide critique: ImageNet results and selection-bias analysis test generalization beyond v2's single empirical dataset, while the literature survey provides an explicit basis for the research positioning. The optimization qualification in Section 4.2 and broader ECDF comparisons also improve the argument's precision and practical usefulness. Losing the batch-size disclosure is a limited documentation regression that does not outweigh these gains.
